sourcedFrom: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet (undated — no copyright line is printed)
cleanIntro: Uberti publishes one leaflet for its whole black powder revolver range and prints two strips in it, one per pattern. This is the Colt open-top procedure — take the wedge out, walk the barrel off the cylinder pin, lift the cylinder clear — followed by the hot-water clean that corrosive fouling makes compulsory.

steps.title: Prove it empty, then clear the nipples
steps.action: Start from the assumption it is loaded. Bring the hammer to half cock so the cylinder will index, then turn it right round and look at all six nipples for caps, spent or live. Anything you find comes off now. Until the nipples are bare there is a primer sitting behind a chamber and no part of this job should start.
steps.caution: Place hammer in the half-cock position.
steps.quote: Rotate the cylinder to see that all the nipples are void of percussion caps. Remove any percussion caps immediately.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — LOADING AND SHOOTING, item 4, p.1 (single-page leaflet, no printed folio)

steps.title: The cylinder does not become safe by leaving the gun
steps.action: If any chamber is still charged, strip the caps off before the cylinder comes out of the frame — a capped chamber can fire while the cylinder is loose on the bench, and there is no barrel or frame around it when it does. Uberti puts this in writing. Go round the nipples a second time rather than trusting the first pass.
steps.quote: Note: If cylinder with loaded chamber must be removed, be sure all (unfired and fired) caps have been removed from the nipples. It is possible for a chamber to fire even though not in the gun. This could cause serious damage to the shooter.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — MALFUNCTIONS, note following item 6, p.1
steps.warn: Treat a misfire or failure to fire as though the revolver can fire at any time.

steps.title: Confirm the pattern before you pick a procedure
steps.action: This leaflet describes its guns by pattern, not by name, and it gives two different disassemblies. Check what sits ahead of the cylinder: a tapered wedge through the barrel lug is the Colt open-top pattern and this gun is one, so the wedge procedure applies. The alternative in the same leaflet is for a solid-frame Remington-pattern gun pulled apart by a T-shaped cylinder pin — this revolver has no such pin and no top strap, so that procedure has nothing here to act on.
steps.aside: Disassembly of the Colt-style revolver (see fig. 1):
steps.quote: All Colt- and Remington-style revolvers are provided with intermediate pins or slots between the single chambers on the rear face of cylinder.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — LOADING AND SHOOTING, note following item 16, p.1

steps.title: Wedge driven out right to left
steps.action: Tap the wedge out of its slot starting from the right side of the barrel. It is tapered and seats one way only, so pushing from the left drives it harder into the lug. Use a punch and light taps rather than prying — the wedge is what sets the barrel-to-cylinder gap, and a bent or burred one will never seat the same again.
steps.quote: Remove the wedge, located just forward of the cylinder, by tapping it through the slot from the right side of the barrel.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — PREPARATION BEFORE LOADING, item 2a, p.1

steps.title: Half cock — the first click you hear
steps.action: Draw the hammer back to half cock, which Uberti identifies as the first audible click. This is what withdraws the bolt from the cylinder notches and lets the cylinder turn freely. If the cylinder is still locked you are either short of the notch or past it into full cock; find the click rather than forcing the cylinder.
steps.quote: Place the hammer in the half-cock position (first audible “click”).
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — PREPARATION BEFORE LOADING, item 2b, p.1

steps.title: Rammer landed on metal, not on a chamber mouth
steps.action: Index the cylinder so that when the loading lever swings down its rammer meets the web between two chambers. Levering there jacks the barrel forward off the cylinder pin. If the rammer drops into a chamber mouth instead you get no leverage and you risk swaging the mouth — on the .44 Army the chamber mouths are what size the ball, so damage there shows up as accuracy loss.
steps.aside: This allows the loading lever to help in removal of the barrel from the frame and cylinder pin.
steps.quote: Rotate the cylinder, so that the loading lever, when lowered, will hit the area between the cylinder chambers.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — PREPARATION BEFORE LOADING, item 2c, p.1

steps.title: Cylinder lifted off the frame
steps.action: Once the barrel is off, the cylinder comes forward off the cylinder pin. Take its weight — a .44 Army cylinder is dense and it will land on its nipples if you let it drop. Note the state of the pin as it comes off: grooves packed with fouling are the usual reason one of these guns starts binding up after a couple of cylinders.
steps.quote: Remove the cylinder from the frame.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — PREPARATION BEFORE LOADING, item 2d, p.1

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, barrel and cylinder are apart, which is as far as this leaflet's strip goes. Now clean it, and clean it today — black powder residue attacks steel from the moment it forms, so a gun put away dirty overnight is a gun that pits. The full wash is in the checklist.
steps.quote: Black powder fouling is extremely corrosive and can rust the barrel and cylinder in a short time. All black powder guns must be thoroughly cleaned after firing is completed.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, item 1, p.1
steps.warn: Warning: Use of smokeless powder in any muzzleloader revolver will result in excessively high presure and can cause serious damage to the firearm and possibly to the shooter.

deepAbsentReason: This leaflet's deeper work is the seven-item CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE wash — complete disassembly, hot water and detergent or black powder solvent, boiling rinse, dry, rust preventative, light oil and grease in the cylinder pin grooves — and it is carried as a cleaning checklist because that is the form the document gives it: a wash routine, not a component teardown. ⛔ NOTHING MODEL-SPECIFIC HAS BEEN INFERRED. The document is a category manual that names no model at all, so no procedure here is attributed to this gun beyond the pattern-level strip it publishes. The nipple wrench and nipple pick appear only within the MALFUNCTIONS misfire drill and are deliberately not presented as routine maintenance.

cleaning.name: CHAMBERS & BORE
tasks: Swab each chamber out with a cotton swab dipped in cleaning solvent
Set the cylinder chambers-down so solvent drains rather than pooling in the chambers
Push a solvent-soaked patch through the barrel, then follow with clean dry swabs and patches through chambers and barrel

cleaning.name: POST-FIRING WASH
tasks: Strip the gun completely and wipe the grips off
Soak the metal in hot water and dish detergent and wipe the fouling off, or scrub it away with a brush and black powder solvent
Rinse in boiling hot water and dry everything thoroughly

cleaning.name: PRESERVE & OIL
tasks: When the parts have cooled, wipe them all with a rust preventative
Oil the moving parts lightly and grease the cylinder pin grooves
Store the revolver dry and with enough ventilation

reassembly: Grease the cylinder pin grooves and slide the cylinder back on.
Bring the barrel back down over the cylinder pin onto the frame, easing it home with the loading lever if it needs it.
Tap the wedge back in from the left until it sits as it did before.
Give the moving parts a light oil only — a heavy coat just traps fouling and makes the next clean worse.
Leave the chamber interiors and nipples dry if you intend to shoot again that day.
fncheck: With the gun empty and uncapped, confirm the wedge is fully seated and the barrel has no fore-and-aft play on the cylinder pin. At half cock check the cylinder spins freely with no dry-pin drag, and confirm it locks up solidly as the hammer reaches full cock. Check the loading lever latches home under the barrel, and confirm the hammer will rest on one of the pins or slots between chambers — the leaflet's own way of blocking the cylinder for carry.
